s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of purpuric lesions with systemic involvement and multi-organ dysfunction
salient_findings: Purpuric lesions on face, elbows, knees, and feet
Skin sloughing off lesions on elbows and knees
Reticulated purpuric macules and patches on extensor surfaces
Dusky purpuric macules and patches on nose, cheeks, forehead, and ear
key_facts: Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear
Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis
Lytic bony lesions on CT scan of pelvis
Hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction, lytic bony lesions, hypercalcemia

shortlist.label: Cryoglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear, purpuric lesions

shortlist.label: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis, abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses

shortlist.label: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses, monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis

shortlist.label: Light-chain amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction, potential for amyloid deposition

raw.rationale: The presence of hypercalcemia, lytic bony lesions, and a hypercellular bone marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction are key findings that strongly support the diagnosis of multiple myeloma. Additionally, the abnormal paraprotein band, monoclonal IgG-κ protein, and elevated serum cryoglobulin levels are consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cryoglobulinemia
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated serum cryoglobulin levels and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear, these findings can be associated with multiple myeloma, and the overall clinical picture is more consistent with multiple myeloma.

rejected.label: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with IgM monoclonal protein, which is not mentioned in the case, and the bone marrow findings are not consistent with Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia.

rejected.label: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance
rejected.why: The presence of end-organ damage, such as lytic bony lesions and acute kidney injury, suggests a more aggressive process than monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance.

rejected.label: Light-chain amyloidosis
rejected.why: While the patient has a monoclonal protein, there is no mention of amyloid deposits on biopsy, which is a key feature of light-chain amyloidosis.
